items.title: Surface flip_budget with every verdict, as the paper's R3 promises (RCP-101)
items.hypothesis: Adding flip_budget (net per-side root-change units, per Theorem 4) to the receipt closes the one place the receipt contradicts the paper, and completes R3's metric pair that conversions_to_reverse half-implements.
items.discriminatingTest: Receipt carries both metrics; I12 extended to enforce flip_budget's formula world-referentially; every pin re-registered; both-implementation reproduction of the new digests.
items.whyItMatters: The paper promises it 'with every verdict'; SCH-005 flagged the absence for KL-011's protected-field survival; the map made the contradiction explicit. Digest-moving -- belongs in the deliberately-versioned family (with BL-026 margin rename and/or BL-037 dependency edges), never in a nothing-moves registration.
items.cost: evaluator change + protocol v1.4/v2 + full re-registration discipline; small next to BL-037, and combinable with it
items.prerequisitesNote: owner decision on the digest-moving bundle's composition

items.title: The paper's untested structural claims (Lemma 1, Theorem 1) need a lineage-bearing schema to test at all
items.hypothesis: A schema carrying parent edges (the paper's actual world model) would let a KL kernel test side-locality and rewiring-immunity directly, instead of I7's declared weaker shadow.
items.discriminatingTest: T1's own statement: rewire parent edges preserving roots and side-consistency; verdict must not move. The map marks both claims not-tested with this reason.
items.whyItMatters: Two of the paper's four theorems are untestable in schema v0.1. This overlaps BL-037 (dependency edges) -- one schema generation could carry both -- and KL-011's transport semantics would inherit whichever model wins.
items.cost: inside the BL-037 schema generation; not a separate build

items.title: TRC-101 applies to every future registration at registration time, not retroactively
items.hypothesis: Extending the preregistration conformance test to require a traceability map (or explicit TRC-101 declaration section) for any kernel that registers a protocol prevents the BRK-101 class from recurring in KL-001..KL-011's registrations.
items.discriminatingTest: A registration without citations or declarations for its normative rules fails the suite before its confirmatory run can execute.
items.whyItMatters: The break survived eight runs in the flagship kernel; eleven kernels are about to write specifications. Catching it at registration costs a map; catching it at IND-style review costs three protocol versions.
items.cost: ~30 lines of test + a TRC section in the registration template

items.title: Paper findings for the owner: PPR-101 (|margin| notation) and the A2 evidence
items.hypothesis: None -- two owner items: fix or leave Theorem 4's redundant bars; and decide A2, now with the recorded paper evidence that the registered reading matches section 3 + section 8 and the alternative has no paper basis.
items.whyItMatters: A2 is the last undecided conclusion-function decision and gates KL-011's transported semantics; the paper evidence lowers its cost.
